title: Expansion of criteria for liver transplants in malignant liver diseases: A policy-oriented analysis within the Eurotransplant network
summary:
Liver transplantation is a life-saving treatment, but far fewer donor organs are available than needed. Therefore, strict criteria determine which patients can receive a transplant. Currently, only selected liver cancers are eligible under narrow conditions.

In recent years, surgical techniques and cancer therapies have improved, suggesting that additional tumor types might also benefit from transplantation. However, expanding eligibility must not disadvantage other severely ill patients waiting for an organ.

Using data from several European countries within the Eurotransplant network, this study evaluates what would happen if transplant criteria were broadened. It examines potential effects on waiting times, deaths on the waiting list, and fairness of organ allocation.

The goal is to provide scientific evidence to support future decisions on fair and effective allocation of donor livers.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm: Intrahepatic bile duct carcinoma
Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct

interventions.name:
Retrospective registry-based analysis of all adult patients listed for primary liver transplantation within the Eurotransplant network between 2007 and 2024, irrespective of underlying indication.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Registration in the Eurotransplant liver waiting list registry within the observation period 01/2007–12/2024
•	Available listing date and defined waitlist outcome (transplantation, death, or delisting)
•	Documented primary diagnosis allowing classification into oncologic or non-oncologic indication
•	Availability of MELD score (laboratory or exception MELD) at time of listing
•	Assignable Eurotransplant member country
Exclusion criteria:
•    Age < 18 years at the time of listing
•    Listing for combined or multi-organ transplantation (e.g. liver-kidney, liver-heart)
•    Missing information on key time variables (listing date or event date)
•    Missing assignment of a waiting list event (transplant, death or delisting)
•    Unclear or unclassifiable primary diagnosis
•    Duplicate registrations of the same listing process
•    Listing outside the defined observation period
